conclusions.result: All nine one-field variants returned native HTTP 400 ConflictException and the original task ARN in resourceIds: omitted count vs explicit 1; count 2; family:revision or family vs full task-definition ARN; reversed tag order; empty overrides object vs omitted; empty startedBy string vs omitted; omitted assignPublicIp vs DISABLED; omitted default SG vs explicit default SG. No client-side rejection occurred; no variant admitted a new task.

Identical replay preserved task ARN but reflected changed task state: initial PROVISIONING/RUNNING, immediately after StopTask PROVISIONING/STOPPED, then STOPPED/STOPPED. Stopped replays retained a full task object including stop timestamps/reason, containers, network attachment, and original two tags; they were not limited to taskArn/lastStatus/desiredStatus in this immediate post-stop observation.

StopTask responses had tags=[] and repeat StopTask returned HTTP 200 with STOPPED/STOPPED. ListTagsForResource on the stopped task returned native HTTP 400 InvalidParameterException: The specified task is stopped. Specify a running task and try again. RunTask replay still included the original two tags.

Changing only cluster to a second owned cluster with the same token and all other inputs unchanged admitted a different task. That task was immediately stopped and reached STOPPED before identical second-cluster replay returned it.

limitations: No long TTL expiry was probed.
No claim is made about untested JSON object key ordering, arbitrary additional fields, or EC2 ENI client-token behavior.
All equivalence variations were tested after the original task reached STOPPED, within the same short-lived token window; identical replay was also tested before stopping.
This is an ECS admission/control-plane probe, not a successfully running workload. Private subnets had no NAT, public IP, or internet gateway.
